searchText: The blocks are more frequent, but they can be missed (unlike PoW). And unlike PoW where an empty block gets made up for by lowering the base fee, under PoS a *missed* block doesn't result in a base fee adjustment. Have there been any stats to see how likely that is? If it’s like our orphan rate then it shouldn’t be significant It could be akin to a mix of EIP-3756 and the Bitcoin halving schedule (or the difficulty bomb): hard-code in a gas limit reduction at a particular date (or cumulative gas consumption). I'm not sure whether a step function or a tapering off would be preferable, but it feels safer to set a lower bound on the upper gas limit (rather than a constantly decreasing upper (gas) limit). The real issue in my eyes seems to be breaking the expectation of 'no changes until the merge is done'. I have wondered whether it'd be ethical to temporarily increase L1 compute costs along with EIP-4488, to create a surge of L2 adoption. Eventually L2 volume will crowd out L1 transactions, and there may be plenty of (economically) stranded assets on L1. The alternative idea of 'Force transfer into a minimal withdraw-only rollup' is also rather attractive [https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/some-medium-term-dust-cleanup-ideas/6287]. It happens when the selected validator is offline for any reason. This strategy is predicated on the assumption that a 10% gas limit increase will have a meaningful impact on gas prices. I'm very skeptical of this claim. I certainly think induced demand will nullify price drops, but there would be greater participation (rather than accessibility). Greater participation should increase value of participating, pushing gas prices a little higher than previously. This reminds me of my city deliberately increasing traffic to reduce road use and bike adoption. One issue is that L2’s aren’t that mature yet. As well, not enough funding/adoption of eth to necessitate the need for L2’s. Crypto still isn’t nearly as big as it should be. The goal should be to keep gas on l1 low until crypto and L2’s are more mature. The demand for censorship resistant programmable money far outpaces our ability to create such things. If you look at the amount of $$ in crypto it’s tiny. And most people using it are buying and holding rather than using. There needs to be a lot more institutional and individual adoption for actual use. As stupid as it sounds you need people paying $1 to buy a cute cat nft to display on their Apple watch. Because that’s how you get them to enter. We are working on it. 😄 I’ve recently become very pro reducing gas 😂 Maybe cause I no longer get it. Funny how once you remove someone's financial incentive for something their views change. 😉 The fact is eth is going to be pretty centralized in staking with exchanges. So might as well increase gas limits cause decentralization isn’t happening. I don't even blame people, I believe it is totally subconscious in the vast majority of people. Totally true Mmm Eth needs to lower fees It cant compete atm And I think if you increased block sizes 10% Gas would go lower by 30% or more For a while until more people use eth Everyone agrees. But doing this *correctly* is years of work. Raise gas burn more fees More transactions at a lower gas price burns the same Have you figured out which wallet the burned eth goes to? All of them. Anyway I get that smaller blocks increase decentralization. I just think with exchanges dominating validation that ship has sailed So might as well make the best of it. We want to fix that, not make it worse. I can’t see that being fixed unless perhaps you introduced a geolocation system like helium that incentivizes people to setup validators at home Right now the cash incentive is to run a bunch of validators on one central server (Not an argument against pos) but realistically it’s just solana with the same central validators. So might as well have large blocks. Any data to back up that claim? Well there’s close to 9 mil eth staked and binance is over 5 million of that I believe? Going by their Beth issuance number of 5.69mil and assuming 10% of that is interest. Then lido at 1.63 mil while decentralized rocketpool is 37,000 Where do you see that issuance number? https://bscscan.com/token/0x250632378e573c6be1ac2f97fcdf00515d0aa91b#balances suggests that the number is significantly lower. Do you mean Venus Beth? That’s a different program I think Given that binance deposit from a number of known addresses, it seems unlikely that they have ~15x their recorded number of validators. Given that their the largest exchange by far you’d assume they would be the biggest validator. On matic their around 15% I believe? I wouldn't assume anything, I try to go by the numbers. And I don't see anywhere your suggested number of validators attributable to binance show up on the chain. Fair enough. Definitely a good chance their numbers are wrong. https://bscscan.com/token/0x250632378e573c6be1ac2f97fcdf00515d0aa91b?a=0xf68a4b64162906eff0ff6ae34e2bb1cd42fef62d Doesn't this say they gave out just 100 973 BETH? Starting balance was 100 000 000 BETH and current balance is 99 899 027 BETH Hmm. That just seems too low to me I’d expect staked eth to be at least 10% given on matic binance is 15%. According to that contract the last out was 371 days ago so could just be that they had beth ready to leave the exchange and not enough has left for bsc so they haven’t claimed more? ah yes. The fact that the token relies on centralized infrastructure makes it very hard to track it. Most BETH probably just sits in user accounts so they didn't record it onchain. This doesn't follow, the main blocker is tooling and exchange support not L1 cost Yeah so to me the 5mil number seems very high but it does seem more probable than the 100k one. EIP-4488 will reduce the L1 costs L2s experience without directly impacting L1 activity costs much at all: the L2s will still be competing for blockspace with L1 activity. If we're able to implement EIP-4488 without advancements in rollup support, why couldn't we increase the costs of L1 activity without advancements in rollup support? Aside from the actual numbers, I'm curious what percentage of people choose Binance because they don't have 32 ETH for solo staking. At least currently solo staking is relatively cheap compared to most services (that typically charge 15-20% of rewards). It's definitely interesting Binance is the exception in that it doesn't charge anything for running your validator (yet), which to paranoid me immediately seems suspicious ;) I afraid though that post-merge the dynamics will change, and that the fluctuating priority fee rewards and MEV will make centralized services more appealing, even if they charge 15-20%. Just realized that PBS might help against this centralization force of validators (right?), at the cost of centralizing block builders I guess. My guess is the majority of eth is likely in the hands of whales. So yes you will have some solo 32 eth validators. But you’ll also have the guy with 10,000+ who just stakes it on an exchange because it’s too much work to run 300+ validators. One huge advantage with exchange/central entities is that they offer 1-1 tokens to represent eth so your not locked up Not sure, people definitely are lazy. There's no real difference in running 300 or 1 validator though. I mean it depends on the economic incentive to solo validate That indeed is very much the case, and for some this is worth the 20% fee. I expect there to be some liquidity providing protocols/contracts eventually as well. But definitely only after withdrawals are enabled, so that'll be a while. Yeh, that's what interesting about Binance I guess, not charging anything. Otherwise you know what you're paying (at least now, not so sure _after_ the merge). I mean binance has never shied away from charging hidden fees before Yeh, I avoid them, but apparently many don't 😅 Anecdotally, I have helped whales set up solo staking with 200+ validators. Amazingly the pattern was "I have an old laptop lying around, I can use that for staking right?" Lol Honestly if I wanted to stake I’d just go buy up Beth or an equivalent rETH It’s at a 5-8% discount usually Please come visit us at the Rocket Pool discord Support decentralized staking and client diversity Yep, if you're gonna use a centralized service like Binance or Kraken, then just buy it at a discount (as opposed to pressing the "stake" button on Binance/Kraken that is). I don't think this option is available to US citizens though, but don't quite remember all the weird regulatory stuff🤷‍♂️ Imagine being in the Eth R&D and considering Binance as your prefered staking service 😅 Money is money I guess 🙂 https://beaconcha.in/pools Some breakdown of the largest pools here Binance is nowhere near majority though Currently there's also no incentive to lock your eth to stake in binance when you can get 6 discount on BETH So it is unlikely for binance's stake to increase Interesting my mistake then A caveat to that stats is that i think the labelling is done manually, so there may be a chance that it is not 100% accurate. But i would assume it is 70% accurate to give a broad picture
